findings.summary: I advised deleting AGENTS.md as stale exhaust. It is the Codex agent-instructions convention AND this repo actively reads it — gate-manifest.json and hooks/scripts/intent_nudge.py both reference it — so deleting it would have broken a live surface. The real defect was narrower: 12 artifacts from a naive Claude->Codex find-replace ('.Codex/' where Codex uses lowercase '.codex/', and 'a real Codex binary' where calibration needs the CLAUDE binary). Caught by David, not by me or any gate.

The Phase 3 sweep applied one blocker prefix to ten entries without reading them and got three wrong (already paid). This pass reads each entry and states a disposition: 1 PAID on verified evidence (--class required, proven in a scratch repo), 13 re-scoped from due-date to trigger (their Done was 'the next live calibration run', which no longer exists as a schedule), 1 retired obsolete (QUARTERLY BUNDLE — its enforcement was the 100-day clock v1.32.0 deleted), 1 half-retired (LAYER_10's engine-side clause is unpayable). Two boundary pins moved with their entries rather than being deleted.

The sweep commit was pushed WITHOUT its review record, so main went RED on the runner between the two pushes. The review-coverage gate is working as designed — a substantive commit must ship paired with its record — but the workflow reality is that the pair has to be ONE push, not two. Recorded so the pattern is visible: this is the second time in the session, and both times CI caught it rather than the local gate, because the local run evaluates the working tree while the coverage check evaluates committed HEAD.
